messages.text:
Trestle Freight is pleased to put a concrete package on the table for Mara:

**Base salary:** $182,000 — positioning at the midpoint of our band, reflecting the platform-ownership scope.

**Signing bonus:** $14,000, payable with first payroll cycle.

**Start date:** We need Mara onboard by early June — ideally June 2 — ahead of a July audit. We can be flexible within the first two weeks of June at most.

**On-site presence:** We'd like weekly site visits for the first 12 weeks to align with the audit prep and team integration.

**Incident coverage:** Business-hours coverage during the ramp-up period, transitioning to a broader rotation once Mara has settled in.

Two areas where I can show flexibility if it helps close this quickly:

1. **Signing bonus vs. start date:** I have some room on the signing figure. If Mara can commit to the earliest start date, I can push the bonus to $18,000. The July audit makes timing genuinely valuable to us.

2. **On-site frequency:** If weekly travel is burdensome, I can propose two three-day visits per month, with all travel fully covered by Trestle.

My questions for your side:

- Is early June achievable, and what would it take to get there?
- Is weekly presence workable, or should we move straight to the two-visit-per-month structure?
- Any concerns on the incident-coverage arrangement?

Happy to hear counter-positions on base salary as well, though I'll note the band is structured around the role level.

Mara can commit to June 1 with the $18,000 signing bonus payable in the first payroll cycle. That would cover the equity she would forfeit by starting before June 15 and give Trestle the earliest start for audit preparation. Please specify any repayment terms in the written offer.

- **Base salary.** We propose $192,000 for ownership of the internal security platform, including accountability for its architecture. If the band limits movement, what base can Trestle approve at this level?
- **On-site schedule.** Two three-day visits per month with Trestle covering travel and lodging works for Mara. We propose that schedule during the first 12 weeks and thereafter, with dates agreed in advance so Trestle can place the visits around audit milestones. Weekly travel is unworkable.
- **Architecture ownership.** Please name Mara as the technical owner for internal security platform architecture, with authority to set design standards, approve platform designs, and shape the roadmap with engineering leadership.
- **Incident coverage.** Business-hours coverage during ramp-up works. Mara can join an after-hours rotation once it has a scheduled primary, a designated and available backup on every shift, and a documented escalation path. Who will staff those roles, and how often would Mara serve as primary or backup? If coverage depends on a future hire, we propose keeping Mara on business hours until that coverage is in place.

We can recommend acceptance once we agree on compensation, confirm architecture authority and the travel schedule in writing, and establish that after-hours coverage has a workable staffing plan.

Several of your terms work as proposed. Let me respond piece by piece.

**Start date and signing bonus:** June 1 with the full $18,000 bonus payable first payroll cycle — agreed. That's the maximum of my signing pool and it's yours because of the audit value. Repayment terms: 100% repayment if Mara resigns or is terminated for cause within 12 months of start; no repayment thereafter or in case of layoff, role elimination, or Trestle-initiated termination without cause.

**Base salary:** I can't go to $192,000. The approved band tops out at $190,000, and I'll offer exactly that — the top of band — in recognition of the architecture-ownership scope you've described. That's the most I can approve at this level without a new internal approval process that would slow us past your June 1 target. $190,000 base plus $18,000 signing is my complete package.

**On-site schedule:** Agreed — two three-day visits per month with Trestle covering all travel and lodging, for the first 12 weeks and continuing thereafter, with dates agreed in advance around audit milestones. Weekly travel is off the table.

**Architecture ownership:** Agreed. Mara will be named technical owner of the internal security platform architecture, with authority to set design standards, approve platform designs, and shape the roadmap in partnership with engineering leadership.

**Incident coverage:** Business-hours during ramp-up, as proposed. On the after-hours rotation: the escalation partner is Devon Cole, our existing senior engineer on the platform team, who will be trained by Mara during the first 12 weeks. Once Devon completes that training, Mara joins the rotation at roughly one week in six as primary, with Devon as backup on those shifts. If staffing changes and coverage gaps emerge, Mara reverts to business-hours until a scheduled primary and available backup exist on every shift — I'm comfortable writing that condition into the offer letter.

To summarize the package for your written recommendation:

- Base: $190,000
- Signing: $18,000, first payroll cycle, 12-month repayment terms as above
- Start: June 1
- On-site: two three-day visits monthly, travel covered
- Title/scope: technical owner, internal security platform architecture
- Incident coverage: business-hours during ramp-up; rotation per the staffing terms above

If that package is recommendable on your side, I'll have the written offer drafted this week.

I recommend that Mara accept once the written offer reflects these terms. Please proceed with drafting it this week.

- **Compensation and start date.** June 1 start at a $190,000 annual base, with an $18,000 signing bonus payable in the first payroll cycle. The bonus is repayable in full if Mara resigns or Trestle terminates her for cause within the first 12 months. Repayment is waived for layoff, role elimination, or termination without cause, and expires after 12 months.
- **On-site schedule.** Two three-day visits per month during the first 12 weeks and thereafter. Mara and Trestle will agree on dates in advance around audit milestones, with Trestle covering all travel and lodging.
- **Architecture ownership.** Mara will serve as technical owner of the internal security platform architecture, with authority to set design standards, approve platform designs, and shape the roadmap with engineering leadership.
- **Incident coverage.** Mara will work business hours during ramp-up and train Devon Cole. Her after-hours rotation depends on Devon completing training and being scheduled and available as backup. Until both conditions are met, Mara stays on business-hours coverage, even if training extends beyond week 12. Once coverage is in place, Mara will serve as primary roughly one week in six, with Devon as backup on her shifts. If a coverage gap arises, Mara returns to business-hours coverage until every shift has a scheduled primary and an available backup.

One addition before sign-off on the offer letter — our travel team has finalized the lodging terms, and there's a scheduling item to confirm.

**Lodging:** Trestle's travel budget funds up to four hotel nights per on-site visit. Since the agreed schedule is two three-day visits per month (typically two to three nights per visit), this fully covers Mara's lodging under the agreed plan. Any nights beyond four per visit would need to be pre-approved by Trestle's travel desk — in practice, our schedule shouldn't produce that situation.

**Second site:** Trestle operates a second facility that Mara will need to visit once before the July audit. I propose folding this into the standing schedule: one of the June visits is designated as a two-site trip — Mara spends two days at the primary site and one day at the second facility, within the same three-day visit window, with travel between sites covered by Trestle and lodging within the four-night allocation.

Questions for your side:

- Does a June two-site visit work for Mara, or would she prefer it in early July (still ahead of the audit)?
- Any constraints on which week in June works best?

Once confirmed, I'll reflect this in the written offer alongside the agreed terms.

June works for Mara. We propose the second half of June for the two-site visit, with two days at the primary site and one at the second facility. Please send the proposed dates for both June visits so we can confirm them together. The four-night allowance works, with Trestle covering inter-site travel and arranging advance approval for any additional night the agreed itinerary requires.

If the audit team would benefit from five consecutive days on site, Mara can extend the two-site visit to five days provided it replaces both planned June visits and the earlier trip is removed.

Please include two timing commitments in the written offer:

- **Travel reimbursement.** We propose that Trestle reimburse covered expenses within 15 calendar days after Mara submits her receipts. If payroll uses fixed reimbursement dates, please specify the submission cutoff and corresponding payment date.
- **After-hours handover.** We propose a handover review at the end of week 12. Mara, Devon Cole, and the platform lead will confirm in writing when Devon has completed training, how Mara reaches him during an incident, and the date of Mara’s first primary shift with Devon scheduled and available as backup. Mara stays on business hours until that handover is complete and returns to business hours if a coverage gap arises, as agreed.

With the June itinerary confirmed and those timing commitments documented alongside the agreed package, I can recommend acceptance.

Trestle confirms both June itineraries as follows:

**First June visit:** Monday, June 9 through Wednesday, June 11 — two days at the primary site (June 9–10), one day at the second facility (June 11). Four-night allowance: check-in Sunday, June 8 through checkout Thursday morning, June 12. Trestle covers inter-site travel on June 11 and advance-approves any additional night required by the agreed itinerary.

**Second June visit:** Monday, June 23 through Wednesday, June 25 — two days at the primary site (June 23–24), one day at the second facility (June 25). Same four-night allowance: check-in Sunday, June 22 through checkout Thursday morning, June 26. Same inter-site travel coverage and advance-approval provision.

On the five-consecutive-day option: we appreciate the flexibility, but we'll keep the two separate visits. Two visits per month around audit milestones is the structure we need, and replacing both June trips with one five-day block would leave the second half of June uncovered.

**Travel reimbursement timing:** Agreed. Trestle will reimburse covered expenses within 15 calendar days of receipt of receipts. Our payroll uses fixed reimbursement dates — the 15th and last business day of each month. So the submission cutoff and payment date will be specified in the offer letter as: receipts submitted by the 10th of the month are paid by the 15th; receipts submitted by the 25th are paid by the last business day. Receipts submitted outside those windows are paid in the next cycle, but never later than 15 calendar days from submission.

**After-hours handover:** Agreed as proposed. At the end of week 12 (week of August 25), Mara, Devon Cole, and the platform lead will complete a written handover review documenting: (1) Devon's training completion, (2) Mara's contact path to Devon during an incident, and (3) the date of Mara's first primary shift with Devon scheduled and available as backup. Mara remains on business-hours coverage until that handover is complete, and returns to business-hours coverage if any coverage gap arises, per the terms already agreed.

The written offer will reflect the confirmed June itinerary, the reimbursement timing, and the handover commitment alongside the full package already agreed. I'll have it drafted for your review this week.

The two separate June visits work for Mara. Please schedule June 9–11 at the primary site and June 23–24 at the primary site, with June 25 at the second facility. That gives Trestle coverage in both halves of June and meets the requirement for one second-facility visit before the audit. Please confirm that itinerary for the letter.

The reimbursement schedule works with the 15-calendar-day deadline applying to every submission. The written handover in the week of August 25 also works. Mara stays on business hours through the handover and until her first scheduled primary shift with Devon trained and available as backup. The agreed coverage-gap provision applies thereafter.

Once the letter reflects that itinerary and the full agreed package, I can recommend that Mara accept.
